newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-KUMBLE SPINS INDIA TOWARDS TEST VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KUMBLE SPINS INDIA TOWARDS TEST VICTORY.

text.p: Leg-spinner Anil Kumble snapped up three wickets to thrust India towards victory in the one-off test against Australia on Saturday.
Kumble removed Mark Waugh, Michael Bevan and Ian Healy as Australia, 179 behind on first innings, slumped to 168 for six at the close on the third day.
The wrist-spinner, who captured four for 63 in the first innings on a pitch that turned from the opening day, took his second innings wickets at a cost of 42 runs in 23 overs.
Only Steve Waugh, unbeaten on 32, remains of Australia's specialist batsmen.
India earlier extended their overnight 319 for six to 361 all out, with wicketkeeper and opener Nayan Mongia finishing on 152, the highest score in any test between India and Australia at New Delhi.
Mongia was eighth out after beating former Australian captain Ian Chappell's record for New Delhi of 138 in the 1969 series.

Chappell was watching from the television commentary box as his score was passed by Mongia, who was bowled through the gate by Paul Reiffel after facing 365 balls during his 497-minute innings which contained 18 fours and one six.
Reiffel claimed three for 35 and was the most successful Australian bowler.
The touring side suffered an immediate setback in their second innings when Michael Slater was dismissed for nought by debutant medium-pacer David Johnson.
When Ricky Ponting was bowled by an in-cutter from Venkatesh Prasad for 13, Australia were 25 for two.
Captain Mark Taylor, batting with confidence, and Mark Waugh repaired the damage to add 47 runs for the third wicket before Waugh was adjudged caught behind off Kumble as he shaped for a square cut.
Waugh, who was unhappy at the verdict of English umpire Peter Willey, made 23 in 80 minutes.
Six runs later Taylor also perished, pushing forward against off-spinner Aashish Kapoor and popping up a simple bat-pad catch to Vikram Rathore at forward short-leg: 78 for four.
Steve Waugh and Michael Bevan then produced the highest stand of the innings, 67 for the fifth wicket.
Bevan made 33 in 93 minutes, including five fours, before he failed to get on top of a vicious delivery from Kumble which went off his glove and thigh pad to Mohammad Azharuddin at first slip.
Healy hit three boundaries for his 12 runs before being beaten by a slower Kumble delivery and was neatly stumped by Mongia.
